body:
I think it might be better here to front-load the behavior warranting the warning rather than explaining/justifying it first. Something like:
```suggestion
				[b]Warning:[/b] Preloaded resources will never be freed, due to a bug in the engine.
```
I'm honestly a bit iffy on including the line about "due to a bug" in general, as it may not instill a ton of confidence in the engine, but it's probably good to keep so that people at least know they aren't doing anything wrong on their end.

body:
I like the idea of the note not telling users to rely on this behavior since it may be fixed/changed in the future, but I think the phrasing "should not be taken into consideration while making your project" is a bit strange. If it "shouldn't be taken into consideration", then why do we mention it at all?

Perhaps a better phrasing would be something like

```suggestion
				[b]Warning:[/b] As of Godot 4.7, preloaded resources will only be freed when the game closes. However, users should not rely on this behavior, as it may change in the near future.
```
Maybe we can also add a suggestion of a better alternative to `preload()` for cases where this freeing-on-close behavior is relevant?
